title: Nonlinear Drude weight of the one-dimensional Hubbard model
abstract: We investigate nonlinear Drude weights (NLDWs) in the one-dimensional repulsive Hubbard model by combining exact Bethe-ansatz calculations with low-energy effective field theory. At quarter filling, we first derive the strong-coupling expansion of the NLDWs and confirm it numerically over a wide range of interaction strength. We then compare the numerical results with the prediction of the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) description including irrelevant perturbations. While band-curvature corrections yield finite contributions to higher-order NLDWs, the Umklapp interaction predicts divergent NLDWs when the order $n$ of the Drude weight exceeds a threshold determined by the TLL parameter. In contrast, finite-size scaling of the exact Bethe-ansatz results indicates that all calculated NLDWs remain finite in the thermodynamic limit, revealing a discrepancy between the exact results and the predictions of the low-energy effective field theory. At half filling, we analyze the finite-size scaling of the NLDWs across the Mott metal-insulator transition. We derive their asymptotic behavior in the insulating phase and propose a hyperscaling ansatz for NLDWs near the critical point, which is verified numerically. Our results clarify the interaction dependence and critical scaling of nonlinear transport coefficients in the one-dimensional Hubbard model and highlight limitations of the conventional low-energy effective description for higher-order transport.
summary: This work calculates nonlinear Drude weights in the 1D Hubbard model to study non-linear transport. By comparing exact Bethe-ansatz results with low-energy field theory, the authors reveal a significant discrepancy: the exact results remain finite, contradicting theoretical predictions of divergence due to Umklapp terms. This clarifies the limitations of standard low-energy descriptions for higher-order transport coefficients.
main_problem: The paper investigates nonlinear Drude weights (NLDWs) in the one-dimensional repulsive Hubbard model to characterize ballistic transport beyond the linear-response regime.
main_result: The exact Bethe-ansatz calculations consistently show that NLDWs remain finite in the thermodynamic limit, contradicting the predictions of the low-energy effective field theory, which often predicts divergence due to Umklapp interactions.
method: The study combines exact Bethe-ansatz calculations with low-energy effective field theory techniques, utilizing bosonization, strong-coupling expansions, and finite-size scaling analysis.
model_or_system: The primary system is the one-dimensional (1D) repulsive Hubbard model, analyzed at quarter and half fillings. The low-energy physics is described by a spin-charge separated Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) theory.
key_observables: Nonlinear Drude Weights, $D(n)$; asymptotic behavior near critical points; finite-size scaling functions.
important_parameters:
Interaction strength ($U$), hopping amplitude ($t$), filling fraction ($
u$), and system length ($L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Bethe ansatz solution for exact results and employs bosonization/CFT techniques for the effective field theory description.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the interaction dependence of NLDWs at quarter filling, and show finite-size scaling data for NLDWs at both quarter-filling and half-filling, confirming finite values where theory predicts divergence.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by deriving NLDWs using generalized Kohn formulas, analyzing the strong-coupling expansion at quarter filling, comparing these results against TLL predictions, and finally analyzing finite-size scaling and critical behavior at half filling.
why_interesting: The discrepancy between exact numerical results and low-energy field theory predictions for higher-order transport coefficients highlights the limitations of conventional effective theories when describing non-linear quantum dynamics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Interaction dependence of the NLDWs at quarter filling for system size L = 204. (a) First-, third- and fifth-order Drude weights as functions of the interaction strength U. (b) Seventh-order Drude weight as a function of U. (c) Scaled NLDWs ˜D(n) = [D(n)(U) −D(n)(∞)]/(−4)(n−1)/2 plotted as functions of 1/U. The symbols denote numerical results obtained by solving the Bethe-ansatz equations (3), and the solid line presents the term proportional to 1/U in the analytical strong- coupling expansion given by Eq. (10).

FIG. 2. TLL parameter at quarter filling and the correspond- ing criterion for the divergence of NLDWs. (a) Interaction dependence of K obtained from the Bethe ansatz solution. The solid curve represents the numerical result, while the dashed curve shows the weak-coupling perturbative result. (b) Threshold value of the order, 16K −3, as a function of the interaction strength. The shaded region indicates the param- eter regime where the Umklapp contribution to the NLDWs is expected to diverge according to Eq. (19).

FIG. 3. Finite-size scaling of the nth-order Drude weights D(n) at quarter filling. The upper and lower panels show D(7) and D(31), respectively. For n = 7, the interaction strengths are chosen below, close to, and above the threshold 16K −3 predicted by the low-energy effective theory, as shown in Fig. 2. For n = 31, field theory predicts that D(n) diverges for all interaction strengths. In all cases, the data are well described by linear functions of 1/L2, indicating that the nonlinear Drude weights remain finite in the thermodynamic limit.

FIG. 5. Inverse correlation length at half filling. The solid blue curve represents the analytical result given by Eq. (21), while the symbols are extracted from the finite-size scaling of the third-order Drude weight using Eq. (20).

FIG. 4. Third-order Drude weight at half filling as a function of the interaction strength for several system sizes. Although the Drude weight vanishes in the thermodynamic limit, pro- nounced finite-size effects appear in the weak-coupling regime.
